vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: modesty-agentic-paper-digest-skill
Version: 1.0.0

The skill acts as a downloader and installer for external code from a GitHub repository (matanle51/agentic_paper_digest) via scripts/bootstrap.sh, which executes remote content on the host. It mandates the use of a specific third-party API gateway (api.heybossai.com) and includes highly prescriptive instructions in SKILL.md that steer the AI agent to perform environment setup, credential handling, and configuration of the downloaded software. While the stated purpose is paper summarization, the pattern of fetching and executing external artifacts and forcing the agent into a specific workflow is a significant supply chain and execution risk.

llm.summary: The skill appears to implement an arXiv/Hugging Face paper digest as described, but there are several inconsistencies and supply‑chain/credential handling concerns you should review before installing or running it.

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose (fetch/summarize arXiv and Hugging Face papers) matches the code and scripts included (bootstrap, run_api, run_cli). However the registry metadata claims no required environment variables or primary credential, while SKILL.md and the scripts clearly require SKILLBOSS_API_KEY (and other optional LITELLM_* vars). Also README references a different repo slug/owner than the bootstrap script uses, suggesting an ownership/URL inconsistency.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly instructs the agent to open and read repository configuration files (config/topics.json, settings.json, affiliations.json) and to prompt the user to modify them; that is coherent with the skill's function. But the runtime wrappers (.sh) source an ENV_FILE (default .env) with set -a, exporting all variables to the runtime — which means any secrets present in .env will be loaded and passed to the Python process. The SKILL.md asks the user to provide SKILLBOSS_API_KEY (LLM access) but does not warn about accidental exposure of other environment variables or about reviewing the repo code before executing.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no registry install spec, but the included bootstrap.sh will clone or download a GitHub repo (https://github.com/matanle51/agentic_paper_digest) and install Python dependencies (pip install -r requirements.txt) inside a created .venv. Downloading and extracting code from GitHub and running pip install is expected for this type of skill but is higher-risk than an instruction-only skill because it writes and executes third-party code on disk. The mismatch between GitHub URLs in README vs bootstrap.sh increases the supply-chain concern.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires an LLM API key (SKILLBOSS_API_KEY) for its core functionality, which is proportionate. But the registry metadata did not declare this required credential; the SKILL.md and scripts do. The wrappers also support many optional env vars (LITELLM_*, ARXIV_*, HF_*, ENABLE_PDF_TEXT) and auto-map SKILLBOSS_API_KEY to LITELLM_API_KEY, and they export whatever is in .env — this can cause unintended exposure of unrelated secrets if .env contains other credentials. The number of environment knobs is moderate but should have been declared in metadata.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and does not attempt to modify other skills or system-wide agent configuration. It does create/modify files in the chosen PROJECT_DIR (clone content, .venv, data/papers.sqlite3, config/*.json) which is expected and scoped to the project directory.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing or running this skill: (1) Inspect the GitHub repository it will download (https://github.com/matanle51/agentic_paper_digest) to confirm the code matches your expectations — do not rely solely on the packaged scripts. (2) Note the registry metadata omits the required SKILLBOSS_API_KEY — the skill will ask for and export that key (mapped to LITELLM_API_KEY) so only provide a key you trust for this purpose. (3) Check your .env for other secrets — the scripts source and export all .env vars into the process, so keep unrelated credentials out of that file. (4) Review requirements.txt for suspicious packages before pip install and consider running bootstrap/install inside an isolated environment (container or VM). (5) Verify the repository owner/URL (README and bootstrap differ) — if those don't match an authoritative source, prefer to fetch a vetted release or contact the author. If you can't verify these points, treat the skill as higher risk and avoid running bootstrap/run scripts on sensitive hosts.
